meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Redwood SE), Jamal Owens (Redwood Product), Jordan Lee (FinSight Head of ML), Samira Patel (FinSight Platform), David Chen (FinSight Security), Rita Gomez (FinSight SRE)
summary: Redwood team walked FinSight through OpenTelemetry instrumentation best practices for token-level metrics and tracing. Main topics: span naming conventions, token-level counters (tokens_generated, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses), batching and batch_latency_ms, trace correlation between client request id and model span, dashboards for token-level cost/latency, and VPC/private deployment considerations for forwarding OTEL data. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share guides and dashboards, FinSight to run bench and share traces; follow-up to review security/RBAC and KMS integration.
topics: OpenTelemetry setup, token-level metrics, span & attribute design, KV cache visibility, batching impact on latency/throughput, quantization tradeoffs, VPC/on-prem OTEL forwarding, dashboards and alerting, security considerations (KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, we'll do a technical deep dive on OpenTelemetry and token metrics, Priya will demo some traces and Marta has a dashboard ready.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: great thanks Alex, um we are mainly trying to get token-level visibility to understand cost per feature and debug high latency requests, so straight to it please.
[00:30] Priya Rao: cool, quick agenda, first instrumentation patterns, then demo traces, then dashboards and queries, then security/VPC questions and Q&A.
[00:44] Samira Patel: just to flag, we run a mixture of hosted and private, so we need both SaaS ingestion and self-hosted collector patterns.
[00:52] Priya Rao: makes sense, we'll cover both. Also sorry for any background noise, I have a dog.
[01:05] Marta Lopez: jumping in, one of our main recomms is to emit two kinds of telemetry - metrics aggregated (counter/gauge) for token counts and latency histograms, and traces for request-level timing and cache spans.
[01:22] Jordan Lee: can you give example metric names? we want to align with our prometheus naming scheme.
[01:28] Priya Rao: sure, common ones we use: redwood_tokens_generated_total, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_batch_size_histogram, redwood_batch_latency_ms_histogram. We also include labels: model_name, deployment_id, region, route.
[01:48] David Chen: how do you correlate a token metric to a user request? we need per-request trace id in the metrics.
[01:56] Priya Rao: great question, we add an attribute on the trace span like request.id and expose the same id as a label on any logs exported. For metrics that are aggregated you can't attach per-request ids, so we rely on trace sampling for deep dives plus per-request counters emitted to a separate metrics stream if needed.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: so for debugging a single slow conversation we would look at the trace and then check kv_cache_hits for that route, right?
[02:22] Priya Rao: exactly. Trace shows spans: client->front proxy->redwood runtime->model engine, inside runtime we emit a kv_cache span that includes attributes: kv.cache_key_count, kv.hit_count, kv.miss_count, prefix_cache_time_ms.
[02:40] Rita Gomez: little aside—how frequently do you see noisy spans? we worry about high-cardinality attributes like convo_id.
[02:47] Priya Rao: good call, we recommend low-cardinality labels for metrics, high-cardinality only on traces and sampled. We also suggest hash_prefix or truncated IDs for dashboards to avoid cardinality explosion.
[03:05] Alex Kim: also worth noting batching can dramatically change token timing shapes. If you look only at per-token averages you'll miss jitter from batching. So we output batch_size and per-batch latency histograms.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: can you demo a trace example?
[03:24] Priya Rao: sure, sharing screen, bear with me. [screen share noise] here's a request with a 1.2s tail, you can see a long wait in the kv_cache span—hit_count zero, miss_count three, and then large model generation span.
[03:45] Samira Patel: that matches what we saw during spikes, sometimes caching was ineffective after deploy. Is there a way to see KV cache effectiveness over time?
[03:54] Marta Lopez: yes, we build dashboards that show kv_cache_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_hits)/ (sum(kv_cache_hits)+sum(kv_cache_misses)) by route and model. We also show rolling windows and heatmaps for batch size vs latency.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: nice, can you share the dashboard json?
[04:15] Marta Lopez: yes we'll share Grafana JSON and a quick-look BigQuery query too.
[04:21] David Chen: security—if we deploy in VPC, can we still ship OTEL out? how does telemetry leave the network?
[04:29] Priya Rao: two patterns—1) self-hosted collector inside customer VPC that scrapes or receives spans and forwards to your observability stack (or to Redwood's ingest if you authorize peered endpoint), 2) outbound-only collector that forwards to a managed endpoint over TLS using mTLS or token auth; for private deployments we support on-prem collector integration and we can also provide a simple forwarder.
[04:56] David Chen: and keys? we need KMS integration and no plaintext tokens in logs.
[05:01] Alex Kim: yes we support KMS/HSM for key storage; the collector configuration can use vault or KMS to fetch send keys. We also scrub secrets in traces and we recommend using hashed IDs in attributes. We'll include our security appendix.
[05:15] Jordan Lee: quantization—does that affect telemetry or trace shapes?
[05:20] Priya Rao: quantization itself doesn't change spans, but it affects per-token compute time so you will see lower model generation spans and slightly different latency variance. Important to tag model_variant and quant_profile as attributes.
[05:36] Rita Gomez: what about sampling rate for traces? we need something economical but useful for incidents.
[05:42] Priya Rao: we suggest adaptive sampling: keep 1-5% baseline global, bump to 100% for requests that exceed latency threshold or error, and always sample requests from key customers/stakeholders. We provide sampling hooks in the runtime to flip sampling flags based on attributes.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: can we see token-level costs on dashboards? our CFO wants cost per feature.
[06:05] Marta Lopez: yes, we export tokens_generated and multiply by unit-cost per model to create a cost metric. It's best to compute cost in your analytics layer (BigQuery/Looker) so you can join with user feature metadata. We can share example SQL.
[06:21] Samira Patel: about batching—we saw in previous tests that larger batches reduce GPU cost but increase tail latency. Any suggested SLOs?
[06:29] Alex Kim: typical tradeoff, we recommend per-route SLOs and autoscaling windows. For interactive routes aim for p95 < 300ms, with small batch sizes, while background batch jobs can tolerate seconds. Redwood's routing can send requests to low-latency pool vs low-cost pool based on route tags.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: can you talk through the trace/span names and conventions we should use so our dashboards match yours?
[06:54] Priya Rao: span naming: redwood.request, redwood.kv_cache, redwood.batch_assemble, redwood.model_generate. Attributes: model.name, model.variant, deployment.id, batch.size, batch.latency_ms, kv.hit_count. For metrics: counters end with _total, histograms with _bucket/_sum/_count per prometheus style.
[07:15] David Chen: any gotchas with OTEL SDK versions? our infra is on 1.12 and some collectors are older.
[07:21] Marta Lopez: we test against common collectors; main compatibility issue is semantic conventions—so include our schema mapping. We'll share a compatibility matrix in the guide.
[07:34] Priya Rao: demo note—here's a token-level waterfall (shows per-token times). It's a mix of model compute and kv lookup; you can see when kv hits nearly eliminate model calls for repeated contexts.
[07:52] Rita Gomez: curious about cardinality again—we have thousands of routes and customers, will labels explode?
[07:58] Alex Kim: we recommend two-layer labeling: fine-grained only in traces with sampling, coarse labels in metrics. For dashboards, use rollups and group_by route_category rather than route_id if you have many routes.
[08:15] Jordan Lee: fine. security-wise, will Redwood persist any PII in traces?
[08:20] Priya Rao: Redwood runtime masks prompt content unless explicitly configured for evals; we strip raw prompt tokens from traces and only emit token counts and hashes. If you need raw content for debugging, we recommend a secured opt-in workflow.
[08:37] Samira Patel: about on-prem private deployment, how do we point our OTEL to your runtime metadata?
[08:43] Alex Kim: the runtime exposes a local OTEL endpoint (unix socket or localhost http) that emits spans; you can run collector alongside. For fully air-gapped, you store metrics locally and then export via secure transfer.
[08:59] Jordan Lee: any sample queries to compute cache hit rate and token cost per feature?
[09:04] Marta Lopez: yes, sample PromQL: sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{route=~"checkout.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{route=~"checkout.*"}[5m]) + rate(redwood_kv_cache_misses_total{route=~"checkout.*"}[5m])) ; cost SQL example also provided. We'll include both.
[09:30] Priya Rao: quick note on tracing correlation—use x-request-id from frontend and propagate. Redwood will pick up http headers: x-request-id, x-correlation-id, user.id (hashed). Keep them as attributes.
[09:44] Rita Gomez: can Redwood auto-instrument our SDK calls? we have custom wrappers.
[09:49] Priya Rao: we have client libs for common languages and examples for custom wrappers; auto-instrumentation is possible but we prefer explicit instrumentation in critical paths.
[10:01] Jordan Lee: what about alerting—what thresholds do you recommend?
[10:05] Marta Lopez: alerts on drop in kv_cache_hit_rate, increase in batch_latency_p95, sudden jump in tokens_generated per minute for a route, and trace error rate. We'll give alert templates.
[10:18] David Chen: last question for now—does quantization change memory metrics we should track?
[10:23] Priya Rao: yes, quantized models reduce memory footprint and per-token CPU/GPU time; track model.ram_bytes, model.compute_ms_per_token, and compare across model_variant. Add quant_profile label.
[10:39] Alex Kim: ok wrapping up, quick recap of next steps: we'll send guides, dashboards, and security appendix; FinSight will run bench and share traces; schedule follow-up.
[10:50] Jordan Lee: thanks all, very helpful.
[10:53] Samira Patel: thanks, looking forward to the dashboard JSON and the instrumentation guide.
[10:58] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[11:02] (call ends)
